title: Impact of ChatGPT on English Academic Writing Ability and Engagement of Chinese EFL Undergraduates
extended_summary:
This paper examines whether ChatGPT can improve English academic writing ability and learning engagement among Chinese EFL undergraduates. The study is not the exact requested paper titled “Impact of ChatGPT on the Academic Writing Quality of Senior High School Students” (2024). Instead, the provided text is a different, clearly identified article focused on Chinese university students, not senior high school students. The match is therefore not exact, and the evidence should be interpreted as relating to undergraduate EFL academic writing in higher education.

The intervention was a 16-week classroom-based use of ChatGPT as a feedback tool in an English academic writing course. Students in the experimental class received ChatGPT-supported feedback on weekly academic writing tasks, interacted with ChatGPT about writing problems, and then revised their writing based on both ChatGPT output and teacher feedback. The control class completed the same course with traditional teacher feedback only. Writing ability was measured using pre-test and post-test tasks based on PTE writing tests and scored by two experienced PTE writing teachers; engagement was measured only for the experimental group using a 20-item Likert questionnaire covering affective, cognitive, social, and behavioral engagement.

The population comprised 70 third-year English-major undergraduates at a private university in China, with 34 students in the experimental class and 36 in the control class. The study took place over one semester in the second semester of the 2023/2024 academic year. The authors describe the design as quasi-experimental plus questionnaire survey. Analyses used independent-samples t-tests, paired-samples t-tests, and descriptive statistics.

The main conclusion is that ChatGPT-supported feedback was associated with greater gains in overall English academic writing ability than traditional feedback. The experimental group improved significantly from pre-test to post-test and outperformed the control group on the post-test. The authors report stronger gains for the ChatGPT group in content, structure, grammar, linguistic range, vocabulary, spelling, and form, while the control group showed more limited improvement, especially in grammar, linguistic range, and vocabulary. Questionnaire results indicated that most experimental-group students viewed ChatGPT positively for affective, cognitive, social, and behavioral engagement in academic writing.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed quasi-experimental study with a comparison group, pre/post testing, and clear analytic methods, which places it above correlational work. However, it is not a randomized trial, uses a small single-site sample, and reports limited psychometric/reliability evidence and no standardized effect sizes, so some credibility concerns remain.
impact_tier_rationale: Findings suggest meaningful positive effects on writing and student engagement, but the study does not report standardized effect sizes or confidence intervals, and several outcomes rely on self-report from a small priority population. Because magnitude is not directly estimable from the paper as reported, impact is promising but unclear rather than firmly established.

interventions.use_case: ChatGPT was used as an AI-assisted academic writing feedback tool in a 16-week English academic writing course for Chinese EFL undergraduates. Students received weekly writing tasks, obtained ChatGPT feedback on issues such as content, structure/coherence, grammar, linguistic range, vocabulary, spelling, and form, interacted with ChatGPT about writing problems, and then revised drafts with both ChatGPT and teacher feedback.

finding.finding_summary: In a 16-week quasi-experimental study with 70 third-year Chinese EFL undergraduates (experimental n=34, control n=36), the ChatGPT group showed significantly greater gains in English academic writing than the traditional-feedback control. Between-group post-test difference was significant (t=3.993, df=68, p<.001; mean difference=1.930), and within the ChatGPT group pre-post improvement was larger (mean gain=3.206, SD=1.067, t=17.522, df=33, p<.001) than the control group's gain (mean=1.250, SD=0.937, t=8.002, df=35, p<.001). Subtrait analyses showed significant ChatGPT-group gains in content, structure, grammar, linguistic range, vocabulary, and form; spelling was reported inconsistently, with table p=.058 despite narrative claims of significance.
finding.measure: PTE-based English academic writing pre-test and post-test scored on content, structure/coherence, grammar, linguistic range, vocabulary, spelling, and form by two experienced PTE writing teachers
finding.std_deviation: EC gain SD=1.067; CC gain SD=0.937; subtrait SDs reported

finding.finding_summary: Engagement questionnaire data from the experimental group only (n=34) indicated that most students reported positive effects of ChatGPT on affective, cognitive, social, and behavioral engagement in academic writing. Positive endorsement rates were generally above 60%, including affective items at about 73.53%-76.48%, cognitive items at 61.76%-76.47%, social items at 67.65%-85.29%, and behavioral items at 61.77%-73.53%; however, no inferential tests or validated scale totals were reported.
finding.measure: 20-item Likert questionnaire on writing engagement across affective, cognitive, social, and behavioral dimensions

finding.finding_summary: Students in the ChatGPT group self-reported perceived gains in higher-order learning processes relevant to durable skills, especially critical thinking/creativity and problem solving in writing. On the questionnaire, 64.71% endorsed that ChatGPT improved their critical thinking and creativity, and 61.76% endorsed that it helped solve problems encountered in English academic writing, though these are perception-based results without objective performance measures.
finding.measure: Self-report questionnaire items on critical thinking, creativity, and problem solving during academic writing
